content_voiceover: This slide covers folate and cobalamin physiology, explaining why their deficiencies behave so differently clinically. Folate is absorbed in the duodenum and ileum, with typical intake around two hundred micrograms a day. Body folate stores are small, only five to ten milligrams, and since daily losses run one to two percent of that store, depletion can occur within just three to six months of poor intake, which is why folate deficiency develops quickly, for example with alcoholism or poor diet. Cobalamin works differently, it binds intrinsic factor secreted by gastric parietal cells and is absorbed in the terminal ileum. Total body B12 content is about two point five milligrams, but daily loss is only about one microgram, so depletion takes three to four years even with zero intake, which is why B12 deficiency from strict veganism takes years to manifest, while gastric or ileal disease causes it faster by blocking absorption. B12 is found in fish, animal products, milk, eggs, and cheese, but essentially absent from plants. Both vitamins converge on the folate regeneration cycle in the bone marrow, feeding thymidylate synthase and dihydrofolate reductase to support DNA synthesis in erythroblasts, which is why deficiency of either one produces the same megaloblastic, macrocytic picture.
keypoints: Folate: absorbed duodenum/ileum; store 5-10mg; depletion in 3-6 months
B12: needs intrinsic factor, absorbed in terminal ileum; store 2.5mg; depletion in 3-4 years
B12 in animal products only — vegans at risk without supplementation
Both feed folate regeneration cycle → same megaloblastic/macrocytic picture
Slow B12 depletion (years) explains delayed onset of deficiency
keypoint_voiceover: Key contrast for boards, folate stores are small and deplete in just three to six months of poor intake, so folate deficiency shows up fast. B12 stores are much larger relative to daily loss, so depletion from dietary lack alone takes three to four years, though malabsorption from gastric or ileal disease works faster. B12 requires intrinsic factor and ileal absorption, and it's found only in animal products, so vegans need supplementation. Both vitamins feed the same folate regeneration cycle for DNA synthesis, which is why either deficiency causes megaloblastic, macrocytic anemia.
